01_benchmark_run_baseline_and_colsweep: GPU: RTX 5060 Ti, 36 SMs, 32 MB L2, compute capability 12.0. Timing = CUDA events, 3 warm-up runs, average of 30 runs, checked against the CPU on 64 rows
Baseline sizes: separate vs fused kernels. At 4096x4096, 0.7020 ms vs 0.3641 ms (1.93x). Every line says MATCH

Row-length sweep, 128 to 8192 columns, five variants. Warp-per-row is fastest on short rows (4096x512: 0.0124 ms vs 0.0268 ms fused); online softmax is fastest at 8192 columns (0.7327 ms vs 0.9704 ms)
02_benchmark_run_blocksweep_and_dram: Block-size sweep, 64 to 1024 threads. The fused kernel at 4096x8192 takes 2.8106 ms with 64 threads but 0.7236 ms with 512

03_benchmark_run_dram_attention_done: End of the block-size sweep (4096x8192, 512 and 1024 threads)
DRAM-bound sizes, three shapes, four to five variants each. Fused reaches 375.5 to 377.8 GB/s, about 84% of the 448 GB/s spec peak. All MATCH
Attention-score shapes (16 heads, sequence length 128 to 2048). At 32768x2048: fused 1.4299 ms vs separate 2.7273 ms (1.91x)
